Continue a defensive win into a controlled transition.
Allow the attack to deliberately create ground-ball chaos.
regressions: Pause between phases to restore organisation.
successIndicators: Protect central territory.
Anticipate spills and imperfect possession.
Maintain useful numbers outside contests.
Force the football towards the boundary.
Select safe, direct defensive disposals.
Create stoppages or turnovers in favourable areas.
Maintain technique and safety under wet conditions.
matchApplication: Wet-weather football increases spills, rushed disposals and repeat contests. Effective defence becomes more territorial, with strong central protection, boundary use and disciplined numbers around ground-level possession.
relatedDrills: TD-052 – Ground-Ball Squeeze and Release Denial

title: Four-Phase Team Defence Match Rehearsal
primarySkill: Maintaining the team defensive game plan through four consecutive match phases.
objective: Develop the team’s ability to move between major defensive phases without losing structure, communication or tactical clarity.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Arrange both teams in full positional structures.
Establish four consecutive phases:
Opposition kick-in
Midfield stoppage
Turnover transition
Repeat inside-50 entry
Nominate defensive leaders in each unit.
The coach controls restarts but provides no tactical instruction during play.
Set a scoreboard and time situation appropriate to the playing group.
Assign assistant coaches to observe separate defensive units.
howTheDrillWorks:
Phase One: The opposition begins with a kick-in and attempts to exit defensive 50.
When the phase ends, the coach immediately starts Phase Two from a midfield stoppage.
After the stoppage possession is resolved, the coach creates Phase Three through an unpredictable turnover.
The teams transition at full speed and play until a forward entry or defensive stop occurs.
The coach then introduces Phase Four as an immediate repeat entry against the defending team.
The defence must reorganise between phases without a huddle or coach instruction.
A successful defensive stop must be followed by an exit suited to the score and pressure.
Complete four to six full sequences before changing the scoreboard or tactical condition.
coachingPoints: Carry defensive communication from one phase into the next.
Defend kick-in possession beyond the first disposal.
Establish pressure, cover and balance around the stoppage.
React immediately when possession changes.
Protect the corridor during open transition.
Reassign opponents rather than searching for original match-ups.
Reset shape immediately after unsuccessful exits.
Maintain pressure and ground-level organisation during repeat entries.
Adjust risk according to score and time.
Retain turnover protection after defensive wins.
Leaders should organise while players are moving.
Complete every phase rather than mentally resetting early.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: Whether kick-in defence protects the second possession.
Whether the midfield stoppage has clear pressure and sweep roles.
Whether turnover reaction is immediate.
Whether the corridor is protected during transition.
Whether opponents are reassigned quickly.
Whether defensive lines reconnect before the repeat entry.
Whether ground-level and aerial contest roles are organised.
Whether player leaders communicate between phases.
Whether fatigue causes structural errors.
Whether defensive exits suit the match situation.

commonErrors.error: Players treat each phase as a separate drill.
commonErrors.correction: Maintain continuous communication and role awareness between restarts.

commonErrors.error: Kick-in defence relaxes after the first possession.
commonErrors.correction: Protect the planned second and third exit options.

commonErrors.error: Players react slowly to the turnover phase.
commonErrors.correction: Change direction immediately and protect the corridor.

commonErrors.error: Defenders search for original opponents during the repeat entry.
commonErrors.correction: Cover the nearest dangerous attacker and communicate new responsibility.

commonErrors.error: Fatigue causes several players to chase the same possession.
commonErrors.correction: Restore pressure, cover and balance roles.

commonErrors.error: Defensive wins are followed by unsuitable risk.
commonErrors.correction: Match the first exit to pressure, score and available support.

progressions: Remove advance notice of the phase order.
Change scoreboard information during the sequence.
Allow the attacking team to select its kick-in and stoppage methods.
Reduce recovery between sequences.
Remove nominated defensive leaders.
Continue all regains into complete attacking phases.
regressions: Rehearse two phases at a time.
Allow 10 seconds for defensive organisation between phases.
Announce each phase before the restart.
Permit one short player huddle per sequence.
successIndicators: Maintain defensive connection through all four phases.
Defend kick-ins and stoppages with clear roles.
React immediately to turnovers.
Protect central space during transition.
Reset after repeat entries.
Communicate without coach direction.
Maintain structure under fatigue.
Win possession and make an appropriate transition decision.
matchApplication: Matches move rapidly between set plays, turnovers, open transition and repeat entries. This rehearsal tests whether the team’s defensive game plan remains stable when those phases occur consecutively without coaching pauses.
relatedDrills: TD-080 – Team Defence Structure and Adaptability Assessment

title: Team Defence Chapter Final Assessment
primarySkill: Applying the complete team-defence system in unrestricted match conditions.
objective: Assess whether the team can independently establish, maintain and adapt a complete defensive system across all major Australian football phases and match situations.
coachingDifficulty: 5 – Expert management of complex scenarios, multiple lines, tactical adaptation and player feedback
setup:
Arrange both teams in full match structures.
Nominate defensive leaders, but require all players to communicate local information.
Prepare a balanced assessment sequence containing:
Slow opposition possession
Fast centre-square launch
Opposition kick-in
Forward-half press
Long down-the-line contest
Full-width switch
Outnumbered defensive transition
Repeat inside-50 entries
Boundary stoppage
Late-game lead protection
Immediate possession-regain requirement
Opposition-specific attacking pattern
Assign coaches to assess forward, midfield, backline and full-team behaviours.
Use a scoring rubric for structure, communication, pressure, contest work, adaptability and transition.
howTheDrillWorks:
The coach begins each scenario without prescribing the required defensive solution.
The attacking team attempts to exploit the starting condition using unrestricted football.
The defence identifies the problem, selects a system and organises responsibilities.
Play continues through disposals, contests, turnovers and transitions until a score, controlled exit or natural stoppage occurs.
Tactical conditions may change during a repetition.
After a defensive win, the team must select an exit or attacking transition appropriate to the scoreboard and pressure.
Failed exits result in immediate repeat entries.
Coaches record outcomes without interrupting normal play.
Players complete a brief self-assessment between major blocks.
The final phase is an uninterrupted match-simulation block in which the defence must operate without coach instruction.
coachingPoints: Establish connected defensive shape before applying unnecessary pressure.
Maintain goal-side positioning and protect high-value central space.
Coordinate pressure, cover and balance around possession.
Adjust defensive depth according to pressure on the football.
Communicate opponent handovers and movement between lines.
Protect the corridor while maintaining weak-side coverage.
Use pressing triggers collectively.
Delay correctly when outnumbered.
Organise aerial, ground-level and stoppage contests.
Create intercept opportunities through influenced disposals.
Reset immediately after unsuccessful exits and repeat entries.
Select between direct accountability, zone, press and delay according to the situation.
Adjust risk to scoreboard and time.
Retain turnover protection after winning possession.
Use player leadership to organise the system.
Maintain legal technique and structural discipline under fatigue.
whatTheCoachShouldObserve: The speed and accuracy of initial defensive organisation.
Connection between forward, midfield and backline units.
Goal-side positioning and corridor protection.
Pressure, cover and balance around the football.
Defensive depth relative to ball pressure.
Weak-side and behind-ball coverage.
Opponent handovers and runner communication.
Recognition of pressing triggers.
Delay decisions when outnumbered.
Aerial, ground-level and stoppage organisation.
Repeat defensive efforts and reset speed.
Tactical system selection and changes.
Scoreboard and time awareness.
Leadership and player-led problem solving.
Contact safety and discipline.
Quality of the first possession after a defensive win.
Turnover protection during rebound.
Consistency under fatigue and repeated phases.

commonErrors.error: Players chase the football without maintaining team shape.
commonErrors.correction: Re-establish connected lines and dangerous-space protection before escalating pressure.

commonErrors.error: Defensive depth does not reflect pressure on the kicker.
commonErrors.correction: Compress when pressure is strong and protect behind when pressure is absent.

commonErrors.error: Multiple defenders perform the same role.
commonErrors.correction: Clearly identify pressure, cover, balance and deeper protection.

commonErrors.error: Runners become free between defensive lines.
commonErrors.correction: Communicate and confirm handovers before responsibility is released.

commonErrors.error: Aggressive pressure has no protection behind it.
commonErrors.correction: Retain a deeper balance layer or reduce the risk of the press.

commonErrors.error: The team fails to reset after an unsuccessful exit.
commonErrors.correction: Recover goal-side immediately and rebuild the structure for the repeat entry.

commonErrors.error: Players use the same defensive system in every scenario.
commonErrors.correction: Select the response according to pressure, numbers, field position, score and time.

commonErrors.error: Defensive regains are followed by rushed disposal.
commonErrors.correction: Secure possession, scan and connect with the safest effective support option.

commonErrors.error: Communication decreases under fatigue.
commonErrors.correction: Require early names, locations and action calls throughout every phase.

commonErrors.error: Players wait for coach instruction.
commonErrors.correction: Empower leaders and nearby players to identify and call the required solution.

progressions: Remove all advance notice of scenarios.
Allow the attacking team to choose how it attempts to break the defensive system.
Change score, time and player numbers during live play.
Use uninterrupted full-match simulation.
Remove nominated defensive leaders.
Require players to review video and grade their own defensive performance.
Assess the team against a different opposition game plan in the next session.
regressions: Assess one defensive phase at a time.
Limit the defence to two available systems.
Allow brief organisation periods before restarts.
Use assistant coaches to guide separate defensive units.
successIndicators: Establish connected defensive shape quickly.
Protect the corridor and central scoring areas.
Coordinate pressure, cover and balance.
Adjust depth to ball pressure.
Maintain goal-side, weak-side and behind-ball protection.
Communicate runners and opponent handovers.
Recognise when to press, delay, match or zone.
Defend aerial, ground-level and stoppage contests.
Recover after broken lines and failed exits.
Reset through repeat entries.
Adjust defensive risk to score and time.
Solve opposition patterns collectively.
Maintain legal technique and communication under fatigue.
Win possession and complete a supported transition.
Operate effectively without continuous coach direction.
matchApplication: This final assessment integrates the complete Team Defence chapter. It measures whether players can organise a full-ground defensive system, adapt it to changing match conditions, win possession and transition without sacrificing the structure required if the football turns over again.
relatedDrills: TD-040 – Defensive Movement Under Fatigue Assessment
TD-060 – Advanced Pressure and Contest Assessment
TD-080 – Team Defence Structure and Adaptability Assessment
TD-090 – Advanced Tactical Team Defence Assessment
TD-099 – Four-Phase Team Defence Match Rehearsal
